record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: If a and b are distinct positive non-integers, then for every ergodic system (X, X, μ, T) and bounded measurable functions f and g, do the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N f(T^{[n^a]}x) g(T^{[n^b]}x) converge almost everywhere to (∫ f dμ)(∫ g dμ)?

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Let a, b be distinct positive non-integers. Show that for every ergodic system (X, X , µ, T) and functions f, g ∈ L∞(µ), we have limN→∞ (1/N) ΣN n=1 f(T^[n^a]x) · g(T^[n^b]x) = ∫ f dµ · ∫ g dµ for almost every x ∈ X.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $a, b$ be distinct positive real numbers, neither of which is an integer. Let $(X, \mathcal{X}, \mu, T)$ be an ergodic measure-preserving system, that is, $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ is a standard probability space and $T : X \to X$ is an invertible measurable map preserving $\mu$ such that every $T$-invariant set has measure $0$ or $1$. For real $t$, let $[t]$ denote the integer part of $t$.

Prove or disprove: for every pair of bounded measurable functions $f, g \in L^\infty(\mu)$, the bilinear ergodic averages
$$ \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=1}^N f\!\left(T^{[n^a]} x\right)\, g\!\left(T^{[n^b]} x\right) $$
converge, as $N \to \infty$, to $\left(\int f\, d\mu\right)\left(\int g\, d\mu\right)$ for $\mu$-almost every $x \in X$.
artifact.category_tag: multiple ergodic averages along Hardy sequences
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (Krause–Mirek–Tao on bilinear polynomial averages, Kosz–Mirek–Peluse–Wright on Hardy field sequences applied to a single function) has advanced pointwise convergence of multiple ergodic averages. However, surveys from 2025–2026 (e.g. "Joint ergodicity – 40 years on") explicitly state that pointwise a.e. convergence of multilinear ergodic averages such as products f(T^[n^a]x)·g(T^[n^b]x) for non-integer a,b remains an open problem, with norm convergence (joint ergodicity) being known but pointwise convergence not yet established.

status_evidence.title: Joint ergodicity - 40 years on
status_evidence.snippet: the pointwise almost everywhere convergence of multiple ergodic averages, a topic first studied by Bourgain over 35 years ago, remains a challenging open problem despite impressive recent breakthroughs
status_evidence.claim: Pointwise a.e. convergence of multilinear ergodic averages of this kind is still treated as open in recent survey.

status_evidence.title: Pointwise Convergence of Ergodic Averages Along Hardy Field Sequences
status_evidence.snippet: averages (1/N) Σ T_1^[P_1(n)] ... T_m^[P_m(n)] f converge pointwise μ-a.e. for Hardy field functions with distinct growth rates
status_evidence.claim: Recent Hardy-field pointwise results concern a single function f under composed transformations, not the bilinear product f·g treated in the problem.
